Subject: Data residency and retention - quick clarifications

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team asked me to get a couple of concrete answers for the vendor review:
- Where will Quantum Health customer data be stored when using Redwood's hosted API?
- What are the retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and customer-provided files?
- If we request deletion, what is the expected timeline for removal from production caches, backups, and analytics?

We have a short questionnaire (attached) but bullet answers here would be great to include in the initial review. Appreciate a concise response so we can move this into procurement.

Best,

Quantum Health

Hi Liam — thanks for the list. Quick answers below; I'm attaching a concise retention matrix as well. Happy to jump on a 20m call if the team wants to walk through specifics.

1) Data residency (hosted API):
- By default customer request payloads and generated tokens are processed in the region you select at account creation. Quantum Health account defaults to US (us-west) for your tenant.
- Short-lived encrypted caches (KV/session caches) live in the same region as processing and are not replicated cross-region unless you enable geo-redundancy.

2) Retention windows (hosted API):
- Request/response logs (for observability and billing): retained 90 days by default; can be shortened to 30 days on request for enterprise plans. Logs are stored encrypted at rest.
- Embeddings and vectors saved via the embeddings endpoint: persisted only if explicitly stored by the customer; by default we do not store embeddings for hosted API calls unless you opt-in. For stored embeddings we provide a configurable TTL (default 365 days).
- Customer-provided files (attachments uploaded for fine-tuning or analysis): retained according to the storage TTL you set; default 180 days.
- KV cache (in-memory/SSD-backed cache used for latency): evicted continuously; keys persist up to 7 days maximum depending on workload before eviction, never indefinitely.

3) Deletion process and timelines:
- Production caches: deletion request triggers immediate eviction from live caches within minutes (SLO: within 15 minutes for standard deletes).
- Primary datastore (tenant records, stored embeddings, customer files): we process deletion requests within 48 hours and propagate deletion to the primary datastore within 72 hours.
- Backups and archival snapshots: backups are on a 7/30/90 day rotation depending on the backup tier; data requested for deletion is purged from new backups going forward and removed from existing backups on the next backup lifecycle pass (max 90 days). We provide an attestation for the purge operation.
- Analytics/aggregates: we maintain aggregated telemetry for service health and product improvement; we do not retain PII in analytics. Any derived artifacts containing customer identifiers are removed as part of the deletion attestation within 90 days.

Security controls: all stored customer data is encrypted using customer-managed keys (if enabled) or platform-managed KMS. Audit logs are available for deletion operations where required.

Attachments: redwood-retention-matrix-2028.xlsx, QH-Security-Appendix.pdf

If you want formal language for a vendor attestation we can provide a one-page statement for procurement to sign off.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen

Hi Asha — quick clarifications below and next steps.

- Billing logs: by default billing and usage logs include metadata (token counts, model id, timestamps) but do not persist full request payloads. For customers on our enterprise hosted tier we can disable payload capture entirely and provide token-level usage only. If Quantum Health requires removal of any historical raw payloads from logs, we can schedule an expedited scrub and provide a one-off attestation (expected completion within 7 business days).

- Deletion attestation: yes — we will produce a timestamped PDF attestation that includes the scope of the deletion, the affected tenant id(s), the deletion request time, and confirmation of propagation to backups and analytics. The attestation will be delivered via the secure SharePoint/DocuSign link you provide or as an encrypted email attachment.

Next steps: I've attached the retention matrix and a short appendix with example deletion language for contracts. If this looks good I can loop in our legal ops to provide the attestation template and we can surface a DocuSign flow for signature.

Attachments: redwood-retention-matrix-2028.xlsx (see sheet: QuantumHealth), QH-Security-Appendix.pdf
